newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH CUP CONTINUES TO THROW UP SURPRISES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH CUP CONTINUES TO THROW UP SURPRISES.

text.p: Montpellier beat five times winners Lille 3-0 away on Sunday to complete a French Cup quarter-final line-up including four non-first division sides following the shock elimination of Auxerre and Paris St Germain.
Forwards Ibrahim Bakayoko, with an eighth-minute penalty, and Christophe Sanchez, nine minutes before the interval, gave 1990 winners Montpellier a 2-0 half-time lead in their third round tie.
Midfielder Fabien Lefevre put the visitors three up in the 66th minute shortly after Lille defender Pascal Cygan was sent off for a second bookable offence.

Holders Auxerre were upset 1-0 at second division Troyes on Friday, while PSG crashed out on penalties to fourth division Clermont on Saturday after going 4-1 up with 22 minutes of normal time remaining.
"I'm incapable of giving the slightest explanation," said PSG's shell-shocked Brazilian manager Ricardo afterwards.
"Today, for the first time, I have nothing to say to explain that," he said after Clermont goalkeeper Olivier Enjoiras saved two PSG penalties in the shootout.

Earlier, Clermont had scored twice in the final seven minutes, including an 89th-minute own goal by France defender Bruno N'Gotty, to level the score at 4-4 and send the match into extra time which yielded no further goals.

"Before extra-time I tried to talk (to the players), but on a psychological level there's no go," said Ricardo, extremely worried about PSG's European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final first leg at home to AK Athens on Thursday.
First division Strasbourg were also upset 1-0 by third division Creteil, leaving Bordeaux, who beat Cannes 1-0, as the only side from the top ten in the first division to reach the last eight.
The other qualifiers were first division Nice and Guingamp and second division Laval, who eliminated first division leaders Monaco in the first round in January.
